page: Google Cloud Platform c4d-highcpu-192 is an x86_64 architecture server instance within the c4d family. It features 192 dedicated virtual CPUs and 360.0 GB of system memory. This configuration yields a memory-to-core ratio of 1.88 GB per vCPU, aligning the instance with compute-heavy resource profiles.

This server type does not include local storage or integrated GPU hardware, meaning all storage requirements must be met via network-attached block storage. Additionally, it does not include complimentary public IPv4 addresses. The lack of local NVMe drives and graphics accelerators represents a clear tradeoff, focusing the hardware resources entirely on raw CPU execution and memory capacity.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the high density of dedicated vCPUs relative to memory makes this instance suitable for workloads that require massive parallel processing power without the overhead of large memory footprints or specialized GPU acceleration. Appropriate workloads include compute-bound tasks such as high-performance computing simulations, large-scale compilation, batch processing, and highly parallelized CPU-bound microservices.
